definition: musical instruments, such as drums, that you play by hitting them.

collocations.example: The drum is a percussion instrument played by striking its surface.
The percussion section kept a steady beat throughout the concert.

definition: to make a hole or holes through something.

collocations.example: Loud explosions can perforate the eardrum and cause lasting hearing loss.
The machine perforates the paper so each stamp tears off easily.

definition: the quality of lasting or staying the same for a long time.

collocations.example: Stone buildings give a city a reassuring sense of permanence.
Spoken words lack permanence, so important deals are put in writing.

definition: allowing liquids or gases to pass through.

collocations.example: Water passes easily through a permeable membrane into the cell.
The soil here is permeable to water, so it drains quickly.

definition: allowed by rules or law.

collocations.example: Such advertising is permissible under the law of most countries.
The noise stayed within the permissible limit set by the city.

definition: to be a perfect example of a quality or idea.

collocations.example: The actress seemed to personify elegance in every film she made.
These volunteers personify the spirit of generosity in our community.

definition: to produce liquid through your skin when you are hot; to sweat.

collocations.example: He began to perspire heavily after running up the stairs.
Workers perspire in the heat of the busy factory floor.

definition: to be connected with or relate to a particular subject.

collocations.example: These rules pertain to safety in the workplace.
She filed all the documents pertaining to the new contract.

definition: to make someone feel worried or upset.

collocations.example: The strange noise did not seem to perturb him at all.
She was deeply perturbed by the sudden change in plans.

definition: to spread through and be present in every part of something.

collocations.example: A sense of excitement seemed to pervade the atmosphere.
The smell of fresh bread pervaded every corner of the house.

definition: a large wild bird with a long tail, often hunted for food.

collocations.example: We were served roast pheasant and vegetables at the dinner.
The hunters hoped to shoot a pheasant in the woods.

definition: a mythical bird that burns itself and is reborn from its own ashes.

collocations.example: The company rose like a phoenix after the financial crisis.
The legendary phoenix is said to be reborn from its ashes.

definition: the smallest unit of sound that can change the meaning of a word.

collocations.example: In English, the letters L and R stand for distinct phonemes.
Changing a single phoneme can turn the word bat into pat.

definition: the study of the system of sounds in a language.

collocations.example: Students study phonology to understand how speech sounds work.
English phonology describes the sound patterns of the language.

definition: strong belief in and respect for God or religion.

collocations.example: Her deep piety led her to pray several times a day.
The old monk was known for his piety and kindness.

definition: to send someone a short electronic message.

collocations.example: Ping me when the report is ready for review.
I will ping a message to the team about the meeting.

definition: the most successful or highest point of something.

collocations.example: She reached the pinnacle of her career at forty.
Winning the award marked the pinnacle of his success.

definition: calm and not easily made angry or upset.

collocations.example: She was a placid child who rarely cried or fussed.
His placid temperament made him easy to work with.

definition: a large flat plate used for serving food.

collocations.example: She arranged the cheese neatly on a large serving platter.
A platter of food was passed around the table.

definition: a flat fold in a piece of cloth, held in place by stitching.

collocations.example: The tailor pressed a sharp pleat down the front of the trousers.
She had to stitch each pleat in the skirt by hand.

definition: to steal goods, often using force during a war or raid.

collocations.example: The invading soldiers began to plunder the conquered city.
Officials were accused of helping to plunder the national treasury.

definition: expensive, comfortable, and of high quality; luxurious.

collocations.example: They stayed in a plush hotel near the city center.
The office had a plush carpet and expensive leather chairs.

definition: (of a vehicle or boat) to travel regularly along a particular route.

collocations.example: Small ferries ply the route between the two islands daily.
Boats ply across the harbor from morning until night.

definition: a strong board made by gluing thin layers of wood together.

collocations.example: He cut a large sheet of plywood for the shelf.
The box was made of cheap plywood and looked flimsy.

definition: a raised platform that a person stands on to speak or receive an award.

collocations.example: The winners stepped onto the podium to receive their medals.
The speaker stood at the podium and welcomed the guests.

definition: causing a strong feeling of sadness or regret.

collocations.example: The old photograph was a poignant reminder of her childhood.
The film's most poignant moment made the whole audience cry.

definition: a strong written or spoken attack on an opinion or idea.

collocations.example: Her essay was a fierce polemic against factory farming.
The author launched a polemic against the new education policy.

definition: to carry pollen to a plant so that it can produce seeds.

collocations.example: Bees pollinate the flowers as they collect nectar.
Farmers rely on insects to pollinate the crops each spring.

definition: a man-made material used for making clothes and other products.

collocations.example: The shirt is made of a light polyester fabric.
He wore a cheap polyester jacket to the interview.

definition: a wild or garden plant with large, usually red, flowers.

collocations.example: The children ran through a bright red poppy field.
She sprinkled poppy seed over the top of the bread.

definition: having many small holes that allow liquid or air to pass through.

collocations.example: Water seeps slowly through the porous rock underground.
The sponge is a porous material that soaks up water.

definition: elegant, expensive, and typical of a high social class.

collocations.example: They celebrated the anniversary at a posh restaurant downtown.
Her family lives in a posh neighborhood near the park.

definition: to suggest or accept that something is true as a basis for argument.

collocations.example: Many religions posit the existence of life after death.
The scientist posited a theory to explain the strange results.

definition: located at or near the back of something, especially the body.

collocations.example: The injury affected the posterior part of the knee.
The doctor examined the posterior surface of the patient's leg.

definition: relating to studies done after completing a first university degree.

collocations.example: She is a postgraduate student researching climate change.
He enrolled in a postgraduate course in economics.

definition: to jump on someone or something suddenly in order to attack or catch it.

collocations.example: The cat crouched low, ready to pounce on the mouse.
The lion waited quietly, then pounced on the deer.

definition: to push out your lips to show that you are annoyed or unhappy.

collocations.example: He began to pout like a child when he lost the game.
She started to pout in annoyance at the decision.

definition: able to be done or carried out successfully.

collocations.example: We need a practicable solution that the team can afford.
The only practicable alternative is to delay the launch.

definition: something that must happen or exist before something else can occur.

collocations.example: A ceasefire is an essential precondition for peace talks.
They set the prisoners' release as a precondition for negotiation.

definition: to decide or arrange something in advance.

collocations.example: The judges should not predetermine the outcome of the contest.
The driver used a map to predetermine the route.

definition: the act of trying to seem more important or clever than you really are.

collocations.example: He spoke simply and without pretension about his success.
The novel mocks the social pretension of the wealthy family.

definition: trying to appear more important, clever, or cultured than you really are.

collocations.example: That is a very pretentious name for a small shop.
His pretentious writing uses long words to impress readers.

definition: relating to basic, deep feelings or needs that seem very old or natural.

collocations.example: Fear is a primal emotion shared by all humans.
A primal instinct told her to run from the danger.

definition: allowed to share in knowledge of something secret.

collocations.example: Only a few managers were privy to the secret plan.
She was not privy to the details of the deal.

definition: acting in advance to prevent problems rather than reacting after they happen.

collocations.example: The company took a proactive approach to customer complaints.
Good managers are proactive rather than waiting for problems.

definition: a doctor's opinion about how an illness is likely to develop.

collocations.example: The medical prognosis after the surgery was very encouraging.
Patients with this disease often have a poor prognosis.

definition: a device that shines images or films onto a screen or wall.

collocations.example: They set up the projector to show the slides.
The teacher connected a video projector to the laptop.

definition: a wide path, especially one built next to the sea for walking.

collocations.example: We strolled along the seaside promenade after dinner.
Shops and cafes line the busy promenade by the beach.

definition: to announce a new law or rule officially and publicly.

collocations.example: The government decided to promulgate a new traffic law.
The king chose to promulgate a decree ending the tax.

definition: a word such as he, it, or they that is used in place of a noun.

collocations.example: The words he and she are examples of a personal pronoun.
In the phrase the man who came, who is a relative pronoun.

definition: correctly describing or predicting what will happen in the future.

collocations.example: His warnings about the flood proved sadly prophetic.
Her prophetic words about the crisis came true years later.

definition: great skill or ability at doing something.

collocations.example: The young player is famous for his athletic prowess.
Her technical prowess impressed everyone in the engineering team.

definition: to move around quietly, especially when hunting or looking for something.

collocations.example: Stray dogs prowl the streets looking for food at night.
The cat likes to prowl through the garden at dusk.

definition: situated nearer to the center of the body or point of attachment.

collocations.example: The muscle attaches to the proximal end of the bone.
Pain was felt in the proximal part of the arm.

definition: relating to the method of treating mental problems by exploring the unconscious mind.

collocations.example: The lecture explained Freud's psychoanalytic theory of the mind.
Her therapist uses a psychoanalytic approach to treatment.

definition: the treatment of mental or emotional problems by talking with a trained therapist.

collocations.example: He decided to undergo psychotherapy to deal with his anxiety.
She joined a group psychotherapy session once a week.

definition: relating to or affecting the lungs.

collocations.example: Smoking greatly increases the risk of pulmonary disease.
The pulmonary artery carries blood from the heart to the lungs.

definition: a large, round, orange vegetable that grows on the ground.

collocations.example: We always eat pumpkin pie at Thanksgiving dinner.
The children love to carve a pumpkin for Halloween.

definition: a joke that uses a word with two meanings or words that sound alike.

collocations.example: He loves to make a pun whenever he can.
We are banking on the loan, no pun intended!

definition: an expert who often gives opinions about a subject in public.

collocations.example: A political pundit discussed the election on the evening news.
Many pundits predict big changes in the housing market.

definition: having a strong, sharp smell or taste.

collocations.example: The kitchen was filled with the pungent smell of garlic.
A pungent odor rose from the old block of cheese.

definition: to kick a ball after dropping it from your hands, before it hits the ground.

collocations.example: The player had to punt the ball downfield quickly.
They chose to punt on fourth down to gain field position.

definition: (of a cat) to make a low continuous sound in the throat to show it is happy.

collocations.example: The cat purrs happily when you stroke its fur.
The kitten began to purr softly on my lap.

definition: an informal word for a cat.

collocations.example: She called softly, here puss, to the stray cat.
A friendly puss curled up beside the warm fire.

definition: to become four times as big, or to make something four times as big.

collocations.example: This year we managed to quadruple the amount we produced.
The small company quadrupled in size within five years.

definition: to feel or show fear.

collocations.example: Many of us quail at the thought of public speaking.
The young soldier quailed before the angry general.

definition: the football player who leads the attack and throws the ball.

collocations.example: The team's star quarterback threw the winning pass.
The defender rushed in to tackle the quarterback.

definition: to stop something, such as fear or unrest, from continuing.

collocations.example: The mayor tried to quell fears about the water supply.
Extra police were sent in to quell the unrest.

definition: an informal British word for one pound in money.

collocations.example: Can you lend me a few quid until payday?
The newspaper used to cost just a quid.

definition: a clever and amusing remark.

collocations.example: She responded to the criticism with a clever quip.
He is always quick with a quip at parties.

definition: arranged in lines coming out from a central point.

collocations.example: The marble floor was laid in a radial pattern.
The seats had a radial arrangement around the central stage.

definition: the branch of medicine that uses X-rays and scans to find and treat disease.

collocations.example: She works in the radiology department of the hospital.
He decided to study radiology after medical school.

definition: one of the sloping pieces of wood that support a roof.

collocations.example: A bird had built its nest on a wooden rafter.
The old roof rafter had begun to rot over time.

definition: a dried grape, often used in cooking and baking.

collocations.example: He had a slice of raisin bread for breakfast.
She added a handful of raisins to the oatmeal.

definition: a complicated or unexpected result of a decision or action.

collocations.example: The new law could have serious ramifications for small businesses.
We must consider the ramifications before making a final decision.

definition: to speak or complain loudly and angrily for a long time.

collocations.example: He began to rant about the poor service at the hotel.
She started to rant and rave when the flight was canceled.

definition: a friendly relationship in which people understand each other well.

collocations.example: A good teacher works hard to build rapport with students.
She quickly established a rapport with the new clients.

definition: the people who read a particular newspaper, magazine, or book.

collocations.example: The magazine hopes to attract a wider readership.
The newspaper now enjoys a growing readership online.

definition: to change the way something is arranged or organized.

collocations.example: The company was forced to realign its operations in Asia.
The crisis made the government realign its spending priorities.

definition: to state or establish something firmly again.

collocations.example: The manager moved quickly to reassert control over the project.
After the storm, calm began to reassert itself in the town.

definition: a sharp expression of strong disapproval or criticism.

collocations.example: His careless remark drew a stinging rebuke from the chairman.
She received a severe rebuke for arriving late again.

definition: to fill a battery with electrical power again.

collocations.example: You should recharge the battery before the long trip.
He stopped to recharge the phone at the airport.

definition: to lean or lie back in a relaxed position.

collocations.example: You may recline the seat once the plane takes off.
She liked to recline on the sofa after a long day.

definition: the act of observing an area to gather military information.

collocations.example: The plane was returning from a reconnaissance mission.
They used aerial reconnaissance to map the enemy's position.

definition: to form or organize something again in a new way.

collocations.example: The board voted to reconstitute the committee next year.
Managers plan to reconstitute the team after the merger.

definition: a priest in charge of a particular church or parish.

collocations.example: The parish rector welcomed the new families to the church.
The rector led the Sunday service at the village church.

definition: to make light or sound change direction as it passes through something.

collocations.example: A glass prism can refract light into many colors.
Water droplets refract the sun's rays to form a rainbow.

definition: an official who keeps official records, especially at a college or office.

collocations.example: The university registrar keeps records of every student's grades.
If you need your transcript, consult the registrar's office.

definition: the physics theory, developed by Einstein, about space, time, and gravity.

collocations.example: Einstein's theory of relativity changed how we see time.
General relativity explains how gravity bends space and time.

definition: to experience something again in your imagination or memory.

collocations.example: Old songs make her relive the happy days of her youth.
He loves to relive the memory of winning the championship.

definition: a period when a serious illness improves and its symptoms lessen.

collocations.example: Her cancer has been in remission for two years.
The treatment led to a complete remission of the disease.

definition: to change the structure or appearance of a building or room.

collocations.example: They hired a builder to remodel the kitchen.
The couple spent a year saving to remodel the house.

definition: an arranged meeting at a particular time and place.

collocations.example: The two spies arranged a secret rendezvous at midnight.
The guide told us to wait at the rendezvous point.

definition: to fill something up again or make it complete again.

collocations.example: The crew stopped at port to replenish supplies.
Staff worked overnight to replenish the stock on the shelves.

definition: an official statement of strong disapproval for something done wrong.

collocations.example: He was given a severe reprimand for his careless mistake.
The officer received a formal reprimand from her commander.

definition: trusted and respected because of a good reputation.

collocations.example: You should buy your car from a reputable dealer.
She applied for a job at a reputable company.

definition: to set something again, especially back to its original state.

collocations.example: She remembered to reset the alarm before leaving the office.
After the power cut, we had to reset the clock.

definition: to seem important or true to someone, or remind them of something.

collocations.example: Her message about kindness resonates with many young readers.
The film's themes deeply resonate with people who have lost someone.

definition: to be filled with a loud, clear, continuing sound.

collocations.example: The hall resounded with applause after the performance.
Her beautiful voice seemed to resound through the whole church.
